open_points.subject: PresuPro transport decision status
open_points.text: “Concrete transport between PresuPro and the portal — decided by R0-09: a bearer header only.” appears under “Unresolved decisions for later states”
open_points.question: Is producer transport closed as bearer-header-only, or is any part of the transport still intentionally unresolved?
options: Treat bearer-header-only transport as final
Treat transport as still open despite R0-09
open_points.default_guess: Treat bearer-header-only transport as final and remove it from the unresolved list.

witness.initial: A later-state author is selecting the producer authentication transport.
events: The author reads the item under “Unresolved decisions for later states”.
The author reads R0-09, which says producers authenticate only with a bearer header.
outcomes: The author fixes the API contract to a bearer header only.
The author preserves transport as an open decision and permits another mechanism.

open_points.subject: Idempotent snapshot replay response
open_points.text: “idempotently returns the existing snapshot” versus R0-25 “answers the import request with that [fresh immutable import] result”
open_points.question: On an identical replay, is the HTTP operation's returned resource the existing snapshot, the new import result, or an import result embedding or referencing the existing snapshot?
options: Return the existing snapshot
Return the fresh import result only
Return the fresh import result containing a reference or representation of the existing snapshot
open_points.default_guess: Return the fresh import result with its new import_id and a reference to the existing snapshot.

witness.initial: Snapshot E version 4 has already been accepted.
events: The same producer republishes byte-for-byte equivalent content.
The portal creates the fresh idempotent-replay import result required by R0-25.
outcomes: The producer receives snapshot E version 4 as the response body.
The producer receives the new import result and its import_id as the response body.

open_points.subject: Administrator project authorization
open_points.text: “Every project-scoped operation checks together: ... access to the concrete project_id” and invariant 2 requires “project grant/assignment”, while administrators manage project assignments and grants “within their administrative area”
open_points.question: What grants an administrator access to a project-scoped access-management operation: a staff assignment, membership in the administrative area, the access-management capability alone, or some combination?
options: Administrators must already have a staff assignment
Administrative-area membership substitutes for an assignment
The access-management capability permits administration of any discoverable active project
open_points.default_guess: Administrative-area membership substitutes for a project assignment for access-management operations.

witness.initial: An active project has no staff assignments, and an administrator has the access-management capability.
events: The administrator discovers the project through R0-08.
The administrator tries to create its first staff assignment.
outcomes: The request is denied because the administrator has no assignment to the project.
The request succeeds because administrative authority supplies project access.
witness.observer: The administrator and the operator awaiting assignment

open_points.subject: Global producer authorization
open_points.text: “a global producer exists only through an explicitly granted capability” while the closed capability set names only “portal.estimate_snapshot.import” and “portal.estimate_snapshot.read_import_result”
open_points.question: What concrete grant or capability makes a producer global, and how is it distinguished from ordinary import capability plus project scope?
options: A separately named global-scope capability
A wildcard producer-scope record
Administrative-area scope covering all projects
The ordinary import capability implicitly grants global scope
open_points.default_guess: Use an explicit wildcard producer-scope record in addition to the import capability.

witness.initial: A service principal has portal.estimate_snapshot.import but no individual project grants.
events: An administrator intends to authorize it as a global producer.
The producer imports a snapshot for a newly created project.
outcomes: Import succeeds because the import capability itself is treated as the stated global capability.
Import fails because no separately named global grant exists.

open_points.subject: Producer allowed source types
open_points.text: “explicit project scope: allowed source types and allowed projects or administrative area”
open_points.question: What are the allowed source types, which snapshot field identifies one, and what happens when the field is absent or outside the principal's allowed set?
options: A closed source-type enum carried in every snapshot
A value derived from source provenance
A property of the service principal rather than snapshot input
open_points.default_guess: Define a closed source-type field in the publication contract and reject absent or unauthorized values.

witness.initial: A producer is scoped to source type PresuPro and project P.
events: It submits a snapshot for P whose provenance names another estimator but whose contract contains no explicit source_type field.
outcomes: The portal derives the source type from provenance and rejects the import.
The portal checks only project P and accepts the import because no source-type input exists.

open_points.subject: Service credential rotation overlap
open_points.question: Who chooses the overlap period, when does it begin and end, and what observable result occurs for the old credential before and after that boundary?
options: A fixed product duration
A deployment-configured duration
An administrator-selected expiry per rotation
Overlap lasts until explicit revocation
open_points.default_guess: Use a fixed or configured duration beginning when the replacement credential is issued, after which the old credential is automatically invalid.

witness.initial: Credential K1 is active for a producer.
events: An administrator rotates K1 and receives K2.
The producer continues using K1 after K2 is issued.
outcomes: K1 remains valid until an administrator explicitly revokes it.
K1 automatically stops working after an implementation-selected interval.

open_points.subject: Viewer access-link issuance and handoff
open_points.text: “authenticates through an unguessable capability link ... issued and re-issuable by an administrator”
open_points.question: What does a successful issue or reissue action return, who is allowed to receive the plaintext link, and how is the link transferred to the viewer when only its verification form is stored?
options: Return the link once to the administrator for out-of-band delivery
Send the link through a named external delivery system
Expose a later retrieval operation
Return only metadata and leave link construction external
open_points.default_guess: Return the plaintext link exactly once to the administrator for out-of-band delivery and never permit later retrieval.

witness.initial: An administrator creates a viewer who has no access credential.
events: The administrator invokes credential issuance.
Only a verification form is persisted.
outcomes: The response reveals the complete link once, allowing the administrator to hand it to the viewer.
The response contains only credential metadata, leaving no specified way for the viewer to obtain the secret.

open_points.subject: Staff suspension and disablement lifecycle
open_points.text: “suspending or disabling an account invalidates its active sessions”
open_points.question: Are suspended and disabled distinct stored states, who may enter or leave each state, may either state be reactivated, and do assignments and credentials survive those transitions?
options: Suspension is reversible and disablement is terminal
Both states are reversible
They are aliases for one inactive state
open_points.default_guess: Model suspension as reversible, disablement as a separate administrator-reversible state, and preserve assignments while blocking their use.

witness.initial: An active operator has an assignment and an active session.
events: An administrator suspends the account.
Later the administrator attempts to restore access.
outcomes: The account can be returned to active with its assignment intact.
Suspension is treated as terminal or equivalent to disablement, so restoration is unavailable or requires a new account.

open_points.subject: Bootstrap administrator audit
open_points.text: R0-07 says creation of the first administrator is “never ... audited”, while “Every significant action records actor provenance” and invariant 12 says “Every significant action carries actor provenance to audit”
open_points.question: Is first-administrator creation an explicit exception to the universal audit invariant, or must it create an audit record with a host/bootstrap actor?
options: Explicitly exempt bootstrap creation from audit
Audit it under a named host/bootstrap actor
open_points.default_guess: Treat R0-07 as an explicit exception and narrow the universal audit wording accordingly.

witness.initial: The deployment contains no staff accounts.
events: A host operator successfully runs the bootstrap command.
An auditor later examines the portal's audit records.
outcomes: No record of the administrator's creation exists, as R0-07 requires.
A bootstrap creation record exists, as the universal audit promise requires.

open_points.subject: Bootstrap command results
open_points.text: “Its outcome is a closed set of exit codes that deployment scripts may branch on”
open_points.question: What is the complete exit-code set, and which conditions—including success, an existing staff account, invalid input, configuration failure, storage failure, and concurrent bootstrap—map to each code?
options: Define distinct codes for every branchable condition
Define success, already-initialized, and generic-failure codes
Expose only success and failure
open_points.default_guess: Define success, already-initialized, invalid-input/configuration, and storage/internal-failure codes.

witness.initial: A deployment script invokes the bootstrap command against a database that already contains a staff account.
events: The command refuses to create another administrator.
The script branches on the exit code.
outcomes: The script receives a dedicated already-initialized code and continues safely.
The script receives a generic failure code and treats the deployment as broken.
witness.observer: The host operator and deployment automation

open_points.subject: Liveness and readiness meanings
open_points.text: “answers an unauthenticated liveness and readiness check”
open_points.question: What conditions make each check succeed or fail, and what observable status or body represents those outcomes without disclosing protected details?
options: Liveness means process responsiveness; readiness additionally checks database and binary-root usability
Both checks mean only that the HTTP process is running
Readiness checks only startup configuration and database access
open_points.default_guess: Liveness reports process responsiveness; readiness requires valid configuration and usable SQLite and binary-storage dependencies, using fixed non-diagnostic responses.

witness.initial: The HTTP process is running but its SQLite database cannot be opened.
events: A load balancer calls liveness.
An orchestrator calls readiness.
outcomes: Liveness succeeds and readiness fails.
Both checks succeed because only process responsiveness is tested.

open_points.subject: Concealed binary-read failure
open_points.text: “An unknown, cross-project, hidden, oversize or unlisted read is answered the same way”
open_points.question: What single HTTP status, headers, and body are returned for all of these failures, and is that response also used when the stored file is missing or unreadable?
options: Uniform not-found response
Uniform authorization rejection
Uniform generic binary-unavailable response
Different internal failures normalized to one externally fixed response
open_points.default_guess: Return one fixed not-found response with no diagnostic body for every listed or storage-level unavailability.

witness.initial: A viewer has access to project P.
events: The viewer requests a hidden document in P.
The viewer then requests an unknown document id.
outcomes: Both requests return an identical fixed 404 response.
Both are concealed but return an implementation-chosen identical 403 or other response.

open_points.subject: Deferred challenge operation responses
open_points.text: R0-23 says a password-reset request “answers as usual”, while confirmation operations answer with “the concealed authentication rejection”
open_points.question: What exact observable response is “as usual”, what exact response is the concealed rejection, and are these responses identical across nonexistent accounts, deferred functionality, invalid tokens, and expired tokens?
options: Always return a fixed accepted/no-content response for reset requests and a fixed unauthorized response for confirmations
Return the same concealed response for every challenge route
Return route-specific fixed responses
open_points.default_guess: Use a fixed non-enumerating success response for reset requests and one fixed authentication-rejection response for every inert confirmation route.

witness.initial: Email challenges are deferred and no challenge records exist.
events: A caller requests a password reset for an existing email.
The caller requests one for an unknown email.
The caller submits an arbitrary reset-completion token.
outcomes: Both requests return the same fixed success response, while completion returns a fixed concealed rejection.
All three return the same concealed rejection because the feature is inert.

open_points.subject: Boundary of recorded snapshot import attempts
open_points.text: “The portal records every import attempt it classifies ... or a rejection” and “An attempt whose bearer credential fails authentication is recorded nowhere”
open_points.question: After authentication, which failures count as classified import attempts and receive an import_id—for example malformed JSON, missing fields, unsupported media type, oversized request, unsupported contract version, unauthorized project, Registry outage, or an internal failure?
options: Every authenticated request reaching the import route gets an import result
Only syntactically valid snapshot commands get an import result
Only domain-validation outcomes get an import result; transport and dependency failures do not
open_points.default_guess: Create an import result for every authenticated, parseable snapshot command; leave transport parsing and internal infrastructure failures outside the import-result model.

witness.initial: A valid producer credential is active.
events: The producer submits malformed snapshot JSON.
The producer retries with valid JSON using an unsupported contract_version.
outcomes: Both attempts receive fresh import_ids because both are authenticated rejections.
Only the parseable unsupported-version request receives an import_id; malformed JSON is an ordinary HTTP error.

open_points.subject: Excluded expense document visibility
open_points.text: R0-18 says “An expense document is visible to the client from its creation; staff may hide it”, while the client view distinguishes included and excluded expenses but does not say whether exclusion affects document access
open_points.question: Does excluding an expense automatically hide its document, leave the document independently visible, or make document visibility conditional on both expense inclusion and the document's client_visible flag?
options: Exclusion does not change document visibility
Exclusion automatically hides the document
A document is readable only when both the expense is included and the document is marked visible
open_points.default_guess: Keep expense inclusion and document visibility independent; exclusion alone does not hide a document.

witness.initial: A newly created expense and its document are client-visible.
events: An operator excludes the expense without changing the document visibility flag.
The viewer opens the excluded expense and requests its document.
outcomes: The viewer can still download the document because visibility is independent.
The viewer cannot download it because excluded expenses implicitly hide documents.

open_points.subject: Registry dependency failures and lifecycle checks
open_points.text: “server-side validation before linked writes, UUID identity matching, typed failure translation” and “Every project-scoped operation checks ... Registry project lifecycle policy”
open_points.question: What Registry failures exist and how does the portal translate each one, particularly timeout/unavailability, unknown project, malformed Registry response, and authorization-independent archived status; may any operation use cached lifecycle or context data?
options: Fail every operation closed on any Registry error
Fail writes closed but permit reads from previously stored portal data
Use a defined cache with freshness rules
Translate each Registry failure to a distinct portal error
open_points.default_guess: Fail writes closed and return one fixed dependency-unavailable error on Registry transport failures; do not infer lifecycle from stale data unless a cache policy is explicitly added.

witness.initial: A viewer has an active grant to project P and P was active at the last successful Registry call.
events: Registry becomes unavailable.
The viewer reads P while an operator attempts to mutate an expense in P.
outcomes: Both operations fail because each must check current Registry lifecycle.
The read succeeds from portal records while the write fails closed.

open_points.subject: Progress-photo publication input
open_points.text: R0-17 says “a progress photo is published the same way” immediately after describing submission of “the confirmed recognition result with the project and the allocation”
open_points.question: Which parts are meant by “the same way”, and what exact prepared-photo facts must staff submit—file_ref or provenance_ref, visibility, caption, section association, capture time, and stable identity?
options: Only authentication and project authorization are shared with expense intake
Photo publication also requires the expense-style confirmed recognition contract
A separate prepared-photo contract supplies a defined metadata set
open_points.default_guess: Share only staff authentication and project authorization; define a separate prepared-photo contract containing stable provenance/file reference, project, visibility, optional caption and section, and chronology timestamp.

witness.initial: A future intake service has placed photo bytes and supplied a reference to an operator.
events: The operator publishes the photo with project and visibility but no OCR recognition result or allocation.
outcomes: Publication succeeds because “the same way” refers only to authenticated staff submission.
Publication fails because implementers read “the same way” as requiring the previously named recognition result and allocation inputs.
